newsitem.title: USA: Polaris sees record 1996 sales, earnings.
newsitem.headline: Polaris sees record 1996 sales, earnings.

text.p: Polaris Industries Inc, reporting lower third quarter profits, said Thursday it expects sales and earnings for all of 1996 to surpass 1995 results.
"While we are disappointed in our third quarter results, we remain on track for full-year sales and earnings surpassing 1995's record levels," said W. Hall Wendel, chief executive.

Polaris, which makes and markets snowmobiles, all-terrain vehicles and personal watercraft, reported third quarter earnings fell to $0.57 a share from $0.67 a year ago. Sales rose to $299.1 million from $291.4 million.
Polaris's 1995 earnings totaled $2.19 on sales of $1.11 billion.
The company said third quarter sales of all-terrain vehicles (ATVs) were 33 percent ahead of 1995 levels.

Offsetting strong ATV sales were slower snowmobile sales. Wendel said the slower snowmobile sales were primarily an aftereffect of a previously reported year-over-year decline in personal watercraft (PWC) sales.

As previously reported, PWC retail sell-through as a percentage of total units available for sale was not as strong in 1996 as in previous years, and some of this year's production is being carried over for retail sale next year, he said. As a result, dealers were not able to take delivery of new snowmobiles quickly, but this situation is expected to be corrected in the fourth quarter, he said.

Wendel said third quarter snowmobile sales trailed 1995 third quarter sales by seven percent. Third quarter net income was also hurt by higher than expected promotional costs related to efforts to push PWC products through the retail pipeline late in the season, he said.
